title: Arsenal’s Riccardo Calafiori, Ben White ‘fine’ ahead of Wolves trip – Mikel Arteta
content:
Mikel Arteta has allayed injury concerns over Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White, suggesting also that Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz have a chance to be involved in the north London derby on Sunday.

The Premier League leaders travel to Molineux to face Wolves on Wednesday and Arteta suggested Calafiori and White should be in contention to play.

“He (Calafiori) is fine,” the Arsenal manager said when asked about the 23-year-old defender at a press conference on Tuesday. The Italy international withdrew from the starting line-up of the 4-0 victory over Wigan Athletic in the fourth round of the FA Cup on Sunday due to an injury.

Arteta added: “He was training with us today, he’s feeling better, and hopefully he’s fit for tomorrow.”

On White, Arteta explained the 28-year-old defender’s withdrawal was due to “a bit of fatigue”.

“He did a lot in the game, and by the end of it, he was feeling a bit of tightness in the hamstring,” Arteta explained. “But he’s fine.”

Norwegian midfielder Odegaard picked up an injury in the draw with Brentford last Thursday while trying to prevent Keane Lewis-Potter’s 71st-minute equaliser, and the 27-year-old Arsenal captain missed the FA Cup tie with Wigan.

“For Wolves, he (Odegaard) is not going to be fit, but for Sunday, we are very hopeful that he can be with us,” said Arteta. “Kai (Havertz) is the other one that again for the weekend is a possibility, so (we’re) looking forward to having him in the squad.”

Havertz, 26, had been expected to miss the derby, so a return in time for Sunday would be ahead of schedule. The Athletic reported on February 11 that the versatile Germany international had sustained a muscular injury and was set for a spell out of the team.

Calafiori has returned to training after withdrawing from the warm-up against Wigan, and Arteta suggested Arsenal were reviewing their pre-match routine. Arsenal have had four players suffer injuries in the warm-up this season: William Saliba, Calafiori (twice), and Bukayo Saka.

“They were all very different,” said Arteta. “The first one was with Willy (Saliba) when he rolled his ankle against Liverpool. Then we had two incidents with Richy (Calafiori) in the warm-up in a really similar way.

“And the other one was with Bukayo, after he was rested on midweek and didn’t play against Kairat, then against Leeds.”

Arteta suggested the problem is weighing on his mind in the build-up to the game.

“I can feel in my body that I’m more aware of it,” he said. “I’m in the office and the moment that I hear my door, and someone stepping in, I’m like ‘no, please!’. It’s a moment that’s really tricky because, for example, if you change Ricky (Calafiori) for Bukayo, you have to change a lot of things within the game plan, positionally there are a lot of things that are different, and you have two minutes to do that.”

“I was a player as well and we like certain routines and that’s the way you tell your body, ‘It’s coming’. It’s a really good area to have a look — what would happen if we don’t do the warm-up? Because then at half-time, we sit for almost 15 minutes, and then we go full gas again in the second half. Maybe something to think about!”

In the absence of Odegaard and Havertz, Arsenal deployed Saka in an attacking midfield position against Wigan, alongside fellow England international Eberechi Eze.

Arsenal go to Wolves with an opportunity to extend their lead in the Premier League to seven points, albeit with Manchester City holding an extra game in hand.
